correctness.rationale: Each voter is unrepresented exactly when every distinct voter in its default-delegation orbit abstains. Exchangeability makes this probability depend only on orbit size. Every local functional component of a path has a one- or two-vertex cycle; decreasing sequence partial sums force extremal cycle placement, and component cost subadditivity collapses all intervals. Exact fixed-count and direct turnout enumeration (see checks/verify.py) checks n=2..9 and n=2..6, respectively; enumeration is corroboration not infinite proof. The two-ended optimizer classification under i.i.d. 0<q<1 follows from strict inequalities.

value.rationale: Physical or trust-network constraints make the predecessor’s all-vertex cycle unavailable. The exact optimum for a path is therefore a natural, previously unreported design invariant: it quantifies the unavoidable number of unrepresented votes, gives the optimal local edge orientation, handles arbitrary turnout correlation subject to exchangeability, and isolates a nonvanishing large-n absolute locality penalty. It addresses a real structural gap rather than a routine parameter substitution.
